title: Cache-aware Task Decomposition for Efficient Intermittent Computing Systems
problem: Energy harvesting IoT devices experience unpredictable power failures requiring frequent state backups to NVM. Write-back caches buffer updates to main memory, creating inconsistent states during backup, while write-through caches increase memory access latency and existing flushing approaches incur substantial backup overhead.
motivation: Energy harvesting is a scalable, cost-effective power solution for IoT but requires efficient intermittent computing mechanisms to handle unreliable power supplies.
method: The paper proposes cache-aware task decomposition that divides applications into multiple tasks, ensuring no dirty cache lines are evicted during task execution while maintaining consistent memory state. This enables parallelization of backup operations with task execution to hide backup latency, leveraging the observation that write-back caches preserve recoverable system state in main memory.
key_novelty: Exploiting the property that write-back caches preserve recoverable states in main memory to enable parallel backup with task execution, eliminating the need for explicit cache flushing before backups.
contributions: Identifies cache inconsistency challenges with write-back caches in intermittent computing
Proposes cache-aware task decomposition to maintain consistent memory states across tasks
Enables parallel backup with task execution to hide backup latency overhead
Validates effectiveness through experimental evaluation with diverse power traces

metrics.other: Effectiveness demonstrated through experiments with different power traces

limitations: Specific limitations and scalability constraints not discussed in the abstract.
